basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 8.' and it opens 'Vers. 8. Tulitque butyrum et lac. Lac cibus infantiae est, ideoque designat veterem'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 8. Tulitque butyrum et lac. Lac cibus infantiae est, ideoque designat veterem legem. Butyrum vero pingue et coagulatum doctrina est evangelica solido cibo sanctos reficiens. Vitulus coctus Christum passum significat. Stabat sub arbore. Arbor crucem significabat, sub qua Abraham stabat, quia mysterium passionis Christi inspirante Deo jam contemplabatur
